description.p: Rill is a small BitTorrent client for GNOME. Paste a magnet link or open a .torrent file, pick a folder, and it downloads.

ul.li: Magnet links and .torrent files, from the add dialog, the file manager, a browser or a drop on the window
Transfers grouped by what they are doing, with progress, speed and peers at a glance
Details of each torrent: a map of the pieces already on disk, its files, connected peers and trackers
Sequential downloading per torrent, so a video can be watched while it arrives
A limit on how many torrents download at once, with the rest queued
Transfers continue in the background when the window is closed, on desktops with a system tray

description.p: The application id is now io.github.sachesi.rill. The dialogs adapt to narrow windows and open as bottom sheets on phones, and the details of a torrent move their tabs to the bottom when there is no room for them at the top.

The add dialog shows the folder a torrent will be saved to. Selection mode has a bar with Resume, Pause and Delete, a search that matches nothing says so, the keyboard shortcuts are listed in their own window, and the context menu of a torrent opens with the Menu key. Changing the number of simultaneous downloads applies at once.

Preferences no longer offer bandwidth limits, an upload limit, a seeding ratio or a logging switch: none of them had any effect on transfers. The Trackers page no longer marks every tracker as connected, and the Files page no longer shows checkboxes that did nothing.

The same torrent added as a magnet link and as a file is one transfer, not two. A torrent you pause is no longer resumed by the download queue, a failed one says so and can be retried, and one that finishes without a final update is shown as completed. Links and files that are not torrents are refused in the add dialog instead of turning into a transfer that never starts.
Magnet links can be dropped on the window, closing the window quits when there is no system tray to reopen it from, and more of the interface is translated.
More reliable tracking of each torrent's state across pauses and restarts.

Ukrainian translation. The source of a torrent can be copied from its details, and its folder opened from the context menu. File paths inside a torrent cannot point outside the download folder, and trackers on link-local addresses are refused.
Database writes and torrent metadata parsing no longer run on the thread that draws the window.
